coverage.landlord_size_condition: The source ties only the private remedies to owners of 16 or more units (portfolio size, not building size). It does not say whether the prohibition itself has a size threshold.
coverage.summary: Prohibits algorithm-assisted rental price coordination in Portland. A 16-unit owner threshold is stated only for private remedies. The source gives no building-level coverage limits.

evidence.quoted_span: for owners of 16 or more units, private remedies include the greater of treble damages or $1,000 per violation
Prohibits algorithm-assisted rental price coordination; for owners of 16 or more units, private remedies include the greater of treble damages or $1,000 per violation.

result.notes: I changed requires_unknown_facts from true to false. The source describes a general prohibition on landlords' algorithm-assisted rent coordination and does not limit it to a class of buildings that assessor data cannot identify (such as subsidized or regulatory-agreement units). I set owner_conditions to null because it duplicated the 16-unit remedy threshold, which is kept in landlord_size_condition with clarifying wording. The only source is a secondary law-firm table entry, so the ordinance's actual scope, definitions and any exemptions are unknown and should be checked against the official text of Portland City Code § 30.01.088.
